enzyme_name: none - spontaneous hydrolysis of the imine released by fructosyl-amino-acid oxidase (amadoriase / fructosyl peptide oxidase, EC 1.5.3.25)
organism_context: fungal/bacterial amadoriase systems (Amadori-product catabolism); MetaCyc assigns no enzyme or EC to this half-step
rationale: MetaCyc pairs RXN-22780 with RXN-22779 (fructosyl-glycine + O2 -> this glycine/glucosone imine + H2O2) and lumps the pair as RXN-22781 under EC 1.5.3.25, so RXN-22780 is the uncatalysed hydrolysis half of an amine-oxidase mechanism rather than a reaction with its own enzyme; the same pattern repeats for the Val, Gln and generic primary-amine Amadori substrates.
direction_note: The imine is a transient oxidase product and its hydrolysis to D-glucosone + glycine is effectively irreversible in water, so ModelSEED's condensation direction has neither an enzyme nor a driving force behind it.

enzyme_name: phospholipid-hydroperoxide glutathione peroxidase (GPx4 / PHGPx)
organism_context: mammalian selenocysteine peroxidase; MetaCyc assigns EC 1.11.1.12 to all of these lipid-hydroperoxide reductions
rationale: GPx4 is a single-domain selenoperoxidase with one catalytic activity, GSH-dependent reduction of a lipid hydroperoxide (here 5(S)-HPETE -> 5(S)-HETE); its sperm mitochondrial-capsule structural role is moonlighting, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Peroxidase reduction of a hydroperoxide by GSH is physiologically irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse call comes from an equation that dropped the GSSG product, which is exactly the term that makes it irreversible.

enzyme_name: unidentified FAD-dependent dehydrogenase of the sibiromycin (sib) biosynthetic cluster
organism_context: Streptosporangium sibiricum; pyrrolo[1,4]benzodiazepine (PBD) pathway
rationale: MetaCyc places this step between reductive release of the carbinolamine from the SibD NRPS (RXN-23235) and TDP-sugar glycosylation (RXN-23241), i.e. a two-electron desaturation of the PBD pyrrolidine ring giving the propenyl-conjugated aglycone; no gene in the published sib cluster has been assigned to it, so I cannot say whether the protein is mono- or multifunctional.
direction_note: Free FAD/FADH2 are written as diffusible substrates in place of an enzyme-bound flavin plus its real terminal acceptor; biosynthetic desaturations of this type run oxidatively and are not reversed in vivo, so eQuilibrator's +14.7 kJ/mol (the basis for ModelSEED's reverse call) is an artefact of the stand-in couple.

enzyme_name: lactase-phlorizin hydrolase (glycosylceramidase / phlorizin-hydrolase domain, EC 3.2.1.62)
organism_context: mammalian small-intestinal brush border; two separate GH1 catalytic domains on one polypeptide chain
rationale: MetaCyc assigns RXN-22888 to EC 3.2.1.62, whose reaction (3) is literally 'a flavonoid-O-beta-D-glucoside + H2O = a flavonoid + beta-D-glucose'; the IUBMB/KEGG entry states the enzyme carries two GH1 glycosyl-hydrolase domains, one running this activity and the other lactase (EC 3.2.1.108), so it is a genuinely bifunctional single chain.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis is irreversible at cellular sugar concentrations and kaempferol 3-O-glucoside is made in vivo from UDP-glucose by a separate enzyme (MetaCyc RXN1F-461, EC 2.4.1.91), so no enzyme runs ModelSEED's glucose + kaempferol condensation.

enzyme_name: unidentified archaeal tetraether backbone methyltransferase (inferred radical-SAM enzyme)
organism_context: Methanomassiliicoccus luminyensis and other archaea producing butanetriol/pentanetriol dibiphytanyl glycerol tetraethers
rationale: Coffinet et al. traced [methyl-13C]methionine into the GDGT -> BDGT -> PDGT backbone series and, because the methyl goes onto an unactivated methylene, inferred a radical SAM enzyme; the gene has not been identified, so functionality is genuinely unknown.
direction_note: Methylation of an unactivated methylene cannot be driven by the SAM->SAH couple alone - the sacrificial second SAM / 5'-deoxyadenosyl radical is missing from the equation - but either way the chain-extension direction is irreversible and ModelSEED's demethylation of PDGT back to BDGT with SAH is not a reaction any enzyme runs.

enzyme_name: MccB, microcin C7 biosynthesis adenylyltransferase (ThiF/ubiquitin-E1 superfamily)
organism_context: Escherichia coli mcc (microcin C7) operon
rationale: The two MetaCyc structures differ only by hydrolytic opening of the N-adenylylated succinimide ring to the aspartyl-phosphoramidate, the closing part of MccB's second ATP-consuming reaction (preceded by RXN-23326, ATP + intermediate 2 -> intermediate 3 + PPi); MccB performs two sequential adenylations in a single dynamic active site, which is iterative use of one adenylyl-transfer activity rather than two distinct activities, and its N-terminal peptide-clamp domain is non-catalytic.
direction_note: Opening a strained succinimide with water is irreversible; the reverse would have to re-close the ring by expelling water, so ModelSEED's direction is not a real reaction. Whether the ring opening is MccB-catalysed or spontaneous is not fully settled in the literature.

enzyme_name: none identified - spontaneous hydrolysis of the clb alpha-ketoimine to the alpha-diketone
organism_context: pks+ (clb island) Escherichia coli; colibactin maturation
rationale: The two MetaCyc SMILES differ only by C(=NH) -> C(=O) between the two thiazoles, and Healy et al. showed that the clb alpha-ketoimine and the related alpha-dicarbonyl are chemically labile and interconvert/cleave without an enzyme; MetaCyc assigns no enzyme or EC, so no catalyst can be named.
direction_note: Hydrolysis of a free ketimine releasing NH3 is irreversible at physiological ammonia levels; ModelSEED's direction would require ammonia to aminate the alpha-diketone, which is not how colibactin is formed.

enzyme_name: gamma-renin (tissue kallikrein-family serine endopeptidase, EC 3.4.21.54)
organism_context: mouse submandibular gland; peptidase family S1 (trypsin family)
rationale: EC 3.4.21.54 is gamma-renin, which cleaves the Leu-Leu bond of the synthetic tetradecapeptide renin substrate to give angiotensin I plus the Leu-Val-Tyr-Ser tetrapeptide - exactly this equation; it is a single-domain S1 protease with one catalytic activity (and note the substrate is a synthetic assay peptide, not a physiological metabolite).
direction_note: Serine-protease peptide-bond hydrolysis is irreversible in dilute aqueous solution; ModelSEED's direction would have the protease ligate angiotensin I to a tetrapeptide.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous hydrolysis of the imine generated by ephedrine dehydrogenase (EC 1.5.1.18)
organism_context: Arthrobacter globiformis / Pseudomonas putida ephedrine catabolism
rationale: MetaCyc's EPHEDRINE-DEHYDROGENASE-RXN (EC 1.5.1.18) makes this imine from (1R,2S)-ephedrine + NAD+, and RXN-21559 is the uncatalysed hydrolysis half that releases 1-phenylacetylcarbinol + methylamine; no enzyme or EC is attached to it, matching the classical Arthrobacter/Pseudomonas ephedrine degradation route.
direction_note: In the catabolic pathway the step runs hydrolytically and is pulled forward by downstream consumption; imine formation from phenylacetylcarbinol + methylamine (ModelSEED's direction) is the industrial/chemo-enzymatic route to ephedrine, not what this MetaCyc entry describes.

enzyme_name: 3-keto-levoglucosan beta-eliminase (LgdB1) plus 3-ketoglucose hydratase/dehydratase (LgdB2, or LgdB3 in some lineages) - two separate enzymes
organism_context: Bacillus smithii S-2701M levoglucosan pathway (lgdA/lgdB1/lgdB2/lgdC); Paenarthrobacter spp. substitute LgdB3 for LgdB2
rationale: Kuritani et al. showed the apparent hydration of 3-keto-levoglucosan to 3-keto-D-glucose is two enzymatic steps - beta-elimination by LgdB1 then hydration by LgdB2 - so no single protein catalyses this MetaCyc entry; each of the two is a separate, monofunctional protein (preceded by LgdA, EC 1.1.1.425, MetaCyc RXN-20952).
direction_note: The beta-elimination that opens the strained 1,6-anhydro bridge is irreversible and commits the anhydrosugar to catabolism, so the net runs toward 3-keto-D-glucose; ModelSEED's reverse direction would have to re-form the bicyclic anhydrosugar.

enzyme_name: phospholipid-hydroperoxide glutathione peroxidase (GPx4 / PHGPx)
organism_context: mammalian selenocysteine peroxidase; MetaCyc assigns EC 1.11.1.12 to all of these lipid-hydroperoxide reductions
rationale: GPx4 is a single-domain selenoperoxidase with one catalytic activity, GSH-dependent reduction of a lipid hydroperoxide (here 17(S)-HpDHA -> 17(S)-HDHA); its sperm mitochondrial-capsule structural role is moonlighting, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Peroxidase reduction of a hydroperoxide by GSH is physiologically irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse call comes from an equation that dropped the GSSG product, which is exactly the term that makes it irreversible.

enzyme_name: AsqJ, Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase
distinct_activities: dehydro-benzodiazepinedione epoxidase, driving the quinolone / quinazolinone skeletal rearrangement
organism_context: Aspergillus nidulans, 4'-methoxyviridicatin / viridicatin pathway; the quinazolinone outcome is substrate-directed
rationale: Einsiedler et al. showed AsqJ excises H2CO from suitable benzo[1,4]diazepine-2,5-diones to give quinazolinones, exactly this reaction; the same polypeptide carries two chemically distinct alpha-KG-dependent oxidations (desaturation then epoxidation) in the quinolone route, so it is bifunctional, though both sit in one active site rather than on two fused domains.
direction_note: 2-oxoglutarate, O2, succinate and CO2 - the couple that makes an Fe(II)/alphaKG dioxygenase irreversible - are all absent from the equation, leaving a formally redox-neutral C-C cleavage with no thermodynamic handle; the enzymology is unambiguously forward, so ModelSEED's deltaG-derived reverse call is meaningless here.

enzyme_name: peptidoglycan glycosyltransferase (class A penicillin-binding protein; PonA1 in mycobacteria, PBP1a/PBP1b in E. coli)
organism_context: most bacteria: class A PBPs fuse both domains in one chain; standalone monofunctional glycosyltransferases (MtgA) and SEDS proteins (RodA/FtsW) carry only the glycosyltransferase activity
rationale: The MetaCyc parent reaction is mycobacterial lipid II + nascent peptidoglycan(n) -> decaprenyl-PP + peptidoglycan(n+1), the GT51 transglycosylase step; in most bacteria that step is run by a class A PBP whose single polypeptide also carries a D,D-transpeptidase domain, which is genuine fused bifunctionality rather than a multi-subunit complex.
direction_note: ModelSEED reduced the transfer reaction to 'lipid II <=> decaprenyl diphosphate', dropping the entire glycan acceptor and product (status MI:C:-40/H:-56/N:-8/O:-21), and EC 2.4.1.129 was transferred to EC 2.4.99.28 in 2023; nonetheless transglycosylation consumes lipid II and releases decaprenyl-PP, so the left-to-right (LLM) direction is the right one.

enzyme_name: phenylalkylamine N-methyltransferase (PaNMT), SAM-dependent
organism_context: Ephedra sinica (shoots); sequence-related to the benzylisoquinoline-alkaloid NMT family of Ranunculales
rationale: Morris et al. isolated the E. sinica NMT that makes (pseudo)ephedrine from nor(pseudo)ephedrine and also N-methyl(pseudo)ephedrine from (pseudo)ephedrine - exactly this reaction; it is a single SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase activity with broad substrate scope, which is promiscuity, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: SAM-dependent N-methylation is effectively irreversible (SAH is a product inhibitor, not a methyl donor), so ModelSEED's demethylation direction has no enzyme.

enzyme_name: phospholipid-hydroperoxide glutathione peroxidase (GPx4 / PHGPx)
organism_context: mammalian selenocysteine peroxidase; MetaCyc assigns EC 1.11.1.12 to all of these lipid-hydroperoxide reductions
rationale: GPx4 is a single-domain selenoperoxidase with one catalytic activity, GSH-dependent reduction of a lipid hydroperoxide (here the bis-hydroperoxide (10S,17S)-diHpDHA -> protectin DX, two hydroperoxides reduced by 4 GSH); its sperm mitochondrial-capsule structural role is moonlighting, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Peroxidase reduction of a hydroperoxide by GSH is physiologically irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse call comes from an equation that dropped the GSSG product (both GSSG here), which is exactly the term that makes it irreversible.

enzyme_name: phospholipid-hydroperoxide glutathione peroxidase (GPx4 / PHGPx)
organism_context: mammalian selenocysteine peroxidase; MetaCyc assigns EC 1.11.1.12 to all of these lipid-hydroperoxide reductions
rationale: GPx4 is a single-domain selenoperoxidase with one catalytic activity, GSH-dependent reduction of a lipid hydroperoxide (here 8(S)-HPETE -> 8(S)-HETE); its sperm mitochondrial-capsule structural role is moonlighting, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Peroxidase reduction of a hydroperoxide by GSH is physiologically irreversible; ModelSEED's reverse call comes from an equation that dropped the GSSG product, which is exactly the term that makes it irreversible.

enzyme_name: CyrJ, PAPS-dependent sulfotransferase of cylindrospermopsin biosynthesis
organism_context: Raphidiopsis (Cylindrospermopsis) raciborskii and other cylindrospermopsin-producing cyanobacteria
rationale: Mejean & Ploux characterised CyrJ biochemically as the sulfotransferase that transfers sulfate from PAPS onto the desulfo precursor, giving 7-deoxycylindrospermopsin; it is a single-activity PAPS sulfotransferase with no second catalytic domain reported.
direction_note: Sulfuryl transfer from PAPS is driven by the high group-transfer potential of the phosphosulfate anhydride and is not reversed by PAP in vivo, so ModelSEED's desulfation direction is wrong.

enzyme_name: unidentified SAM-dependent 2-deoxystreptamine N-methyltransferase (hyosamine-forming) of the hygromycin B / destomycin aminocyclitol pathway
organism_context: Streptomyces hygroscopicus and relatives; MetaCyc then glycosylates hyosamine (RXN-23143, EC 2.4.1.-)
rationale: Hyosamine is N-methyl-2-deoxystreptamine and MetaCyc assigns only a partial EC (2.1.1.-) with no gene; PubMed/Europe PMC searches returned no characterised enzyme for this methylation, so I cannot judge mono- vs multifunctionality.
direction_note: Whatever protein runs it, SAM-dependent N-methylation is irreversible, so ModelSEED's demethylation of hyosamine back to 2-deoxystreptamine is not a real reaction.

enzyme_name: Asm21, ansamitocin O-carbamoyltransferase
organism_context: Actinosynnema pretiosum; homodimeric carbamoyltransferase family (cf. GdmN in geldanamycin biosynthesis)
rationale: Li et al. showed Asm21 carbamoylates both the C-7 hydroxyl of the ansamitocin polyketide and the 4''-OH of the glycosyl moiety - the same carbamoyl-transfer chemistry used iteratively at two sites, not two distinct catalytic activities; its close homologue GdmN behaves the same way, and the active enzyme is a homodimer, not a fused multidomain chain.
direction_note: Carbamoyl transfer from carbamoyl phosphate is pulled forward by inorganic-phosphate release and is not reversed in vivo, so ModelSEED's decarbamoylation direction has no enzyme.
